alignments.note: Interrogative takes the fronted question auxiliary (rule 17).
Anarthrous substantive with supplied a/man (rules 15, 46); head on wise.

Light verb make + complement answer heads on answer (rule 44). דַעַת is the accusative object of עָנָה, so the supplied with the English verb phrase needs to reach it is the verb's under rule 44's direct-object clause, exactly as 'have done violence to my law'; the prior reading gave with to the noun as an adverbial accusative under rule 33, but rule 33 defers to rule 44 where a verb governs the noun.
Object noun keeps only its own word; the with belongs to the verb (rule 44).
Rectum rendered attributively (rule 28); margin gloss read and set aside (rule 38).

מָלֵא piel governs קָדִים as its second accusative, and English 'fill … with' admits no other word before that complement, so the with is the verb's on both rule 44's direct-object clause and rule 33's valency test (cf. מָלֵא דָשֶׁן → full of); discontinuous around himself (rule 25). Prior reading gave with to the noun.
Noun takes the supplied the (rule 15); head on wind as the class noun the ASV writes alone for רוּחַ, east being the specifier (rule 31), though east was also defensible.
'his belly' recast as reflexive himself; one English word for noun+suffix (rule 30), headed on the suffix whose pronoun it writes. Competing reading: noun unrepresented.

review_notes: Corrected: both supplied withs moved from the bare nouns to the verbs whose objects they reach (rule 44); margin gloss 'knowledge of wind' read and set aside (rule 38).
